modules.title: What GENESIS does
modules.intro: GENESIS runs on your own Linux server, next to your Cadence tools and licenses. Your engineers use it in the browser.

items.title: Passive synthesis
items.detail: Draw the pixel area, place the ports and set S-parameter goals. GENESIS searches layouts for baluns, power dividers, couplers, filters and other N-port structures, and checks each candidate with your EM solver.

items.title: Optimization
items.detail: Choose evolutionary, Bayesian or reinforcement-learning search, run many EM simulations in parallel, compare the trade-offs on a Pareto front and download the best layout as GDS.

items.title: Active circuits
items.detail: Open a Cadence schematic, set its design variables and run Spectre analyses such as S-parameters, noise, harmonic balance and stability. Tune the variables toward S-parameter targets.

items.title: Composer
items.detail: Place active stages and passive structures on one canvas, connect their ports, run each block and export the design to Cadence as a library with testbenches.

items.title: Design assistant
items.detail: Describe what you want to design. The assistant opens the right tool with a first setup and can start and follow an optimization for you.

items.title: Results and scripting
items.detail: Every run keeps its settings, responses and GDS files, so you can compare runs and continue from earlier work. What you do in the interface can also be run from Python.

story.headline: Why we’re building GENESIS.
story.intro: We bring together RFIC research and experience in building AI products. Our shared aim is to connect the parts of the design process that too often happen in isolation.
paragraphs: Changing a circuit is only one part of the job. Engineers also need to prepare the next simulation, compare it with earlier runs and check what the change means for the physical design.

We are building GENESIS so that this process does not need to be reconstructed with every iteration. Engineers should be able to focus on the circuit, and carry the settings and results of earlier work into their next design.

loop.caption: The GENESIS design loop: from your target to a layout that meets it.

steps.title: Set the target
steps.detail: You define the frequency band, the allowed loss and where the ports sit.

steps.title: GENESIS proposes a layout
steps.detail: It generates a candidate geometry for your process.

steps.title: Your EM solver checks it
steps.detail: A full-wave simulation returns the real response.

steps.title: Compare and refine
steps.detail: GENESIS learns from the gap and proposes a better candidate.

steps.title: Target met
steps.detail: The best candidate moves on to layout and verification.
